<SUMMARY>The period of June 5-12, 2026, saw significant geopolitical developments, notably the digital signing of a framework peace deal between the United States and Iran, aiming to end a three-month-long conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. This agreement led to a surge in global stock markets and a drop in oil prices. Concurrently, the Trump administration intensified its export controls on advanced AI models, specifically placing Anthropic’s Fable 5 AI model under restrictions, affecting foreign access including for a China-linked Korean telecom and raising alarms about structural dependence for European organizations. The semiconductor industry continued to see strategic investments and supply chain restructuring efforts, with TSMC and Amkor signing a 10-year advanced packaging deal in Arizona and Nokia expanding US semiconductor operations. Critical minerals also remained a strategic focus, with US initiatives targeting African resources and European funding for alternative solutions.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>The US export control on Anthropic’s Fable 5 AI model highlights a growing risk of structural dependence for European organizations on US AI labs. Severe NAND shortages are projected to worsen in 2027 as AI data centers increasingly consume supply. The use of Musk’s Grok AI tool to guide US strikes on Iran reveals the increasing integration of advanced AI into military operations, raising new ethical and strategic considerations.</EWS>
<EXEC>

**Asia:** Huawei’s new Kirin SoC in the Mate 90 series is said to match TSMC’s 3nm node despite lacking access to EUV equipment, demonstrating continued competitive advancements. Taiwan's AI supply chain posted triple-digit gains in May, driven by server makers and memory chips. The US blocked foreign access to Anthropic AI, specifically over suspected China-linked Korean Telecom involvement. China's energy strategy is being affected by the US-Iran peace deal. China is formulating a response to Europe's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).

**Africa:** Essar Group and IRH plan to establish a $500 million crude oil and product sourcing facility.

**Europe:** The European Parliament ratified the Turnberry Agreement, a trade deal with the United States, with 440 votes in favour, 151 against, and 50 abstentions, eliminating duties. The EU Foreign Affairs Council imposed new sanctions against Russia. Infineon announced plans to open a new fab in Germany to support sovereignty pushes. Intel began production of anticipated 18A-P chips, driven by AI demand. Bitcoin miner IREN acquired Spain’s Nostrum Group, securing 490MW of grid-connected power to boost its AI strategy. Poland is pursuing investments and technology transfers from Taiwanese companies to reengineer its economy.

**Americas:** TSMC and Amkor signed a 10-year deal to expand semiconductor packaging in Arizona, aiming to strengthen the US semiconductor supply chain and reduce reliance on Asia. Oracle is investing tens of billions into cloud infrastructure for AI workloads globally. Qualcomm is reportedly in talks to acquire RISC-V-based AI accelerator and CPU developer Tenstorrent for $8 billion to $10 billion. Intel and NVIDIA are collaborating on Serpent Lake SoCs, integrating RTX graphics for enhanced AI and computing performance, targeting an early 2028 debut. President Donald Trump’s administration placed Anthropic’s Fable 5 AI model under export control, highlighting a risk of structural dependence for European organizations and blocking foreign access for a China-linked Korean Telecom. Nokia announced a major expansion of its US semiconductor advanced test and packaging operations in Pennsylvania to bolster AI growth. Samsung faces foundry capacity shortages, prompting Google, AMD, and Tesla to seek partnerships.</EXEC>
<LITHO>

**Asia:** Huawei claims its new Kirin SoC in the Mate 90 series, set for later this year, matches TSMC’s 3nm node despite the company's lack of access to the latest EUV equipment.

**Europe:** ASML is experiencing a record order book, riding the wave of AI infrastructure trades. Imec is advancing quantum technology towards manufacturable silicon systems.</LITHO>
<REE>

**Africa:** America’s New Critical Minerals Playbook is being implemented, focusing on securing resources in Africa. The race for East Africa’s critical minerals is impacting regional conservation efforts. A dispute concerning colonial-era geological maps between DR Congo and Belgium has been explained in the context of critical minerals.

**Europe:** The EQT Foundation has awarded over €1 Million in grants to researchers from 11 institutions across 9 countries for developing alternatives to critical minerals used in batteries, hydrogen, solar, and industrial systems.

**Americas:** Metallium Limited announced the successful completion of multi-unit Flash Joule heating operations at its technology development facility in Texas. Eagle Nuclear Energy Corp. is building across both ends of the domestic fuel supply chain, addressing a missing link in America's nuclear comeback ignited by AI data centers and electrification. Purebase Corporation established a “mine to market” relationship with CoreTer LLC. Brixton Metals Corporation reported drilling 906 g/t Silver over 4.3 m, including 1,329 g/t Silver over 1.8 m, all within 23.7 m of 206.6 g/t Silver at its Langis Project, located in Canada.</REE>
<GEO>

**Asia:** The US-Iran peace deal has rattled China’s energy strategy and geopolitics. China is formulating its response to Europe's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).

**Europe:** Poland is pursuing a flood of investments and technology transfers from Taiwanese companies as part of its strategy to reengineer its economy. The EU Foreign Affairs Council stated that new sanctions against Russia send a clear signal, and Russia will not achieve its imperialist ambitions.</GEO>
<MILITARY>

**Americas:** Defense data centers are becoming critical infrastructure for global military power due to the rapid progress of artificial intelligence, cybersecurity measures, and autonomous systems reshaping modern warfare.

**West Asia:** Musk’s Grok AI tool helped guide US strikes on Iran, as revealed in a legal briefing. The Pentagon confirmed that Musk’s AI, Grok, was used in strikes in Iran.</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>The geopolitical landscape is currently being reshaped by significant diplomatic breakthroughs in West Asia, leading to immediate economic impacts. Simultaneously, the global competition in advanced technologies, particularly AI and semiconductors, is intensifying, characterized by strategic investments, supply chain diversification efforts, and growing export controls. The reliance on critical minerals for energy security and technological advancement remains a central focus for various nations, driving new exploration and alternative material research.</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>ISRO scientists launched the Space Technology & Research Program 2026 at Chandigarh University. India is actively exploring rare earth supplies from Russia’s Tomtor deposit in Siberia, aiming to reduce dependence on China and secure critical minerals. The AI-Driven Ion Exchange Materials Market attracted $73 million in investment funding. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu invited global semiconductor manufacturers to invest in the state, highlighting plans for a semiconductor manufacturing facility in the Rayalaseema region. Meta-Reliance is developing AI data centers, and Anthropic has formed a tie-up with TCS. Indian shares closed higher, with the Sensex gaining 544 points and the Nifty settling at 23,989, following the preliminary US-Iran peace deal, which cooled oil prices and improved risk appetite.</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>The United States and Iran digitally signed a framework deal to end the three-month-long war and facilitate the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump stated in a G7 memo that Iran will not have a nuclear weapon. Qatar is preparing to quickly restart and restore liquefied natural gas output within weeks once the Strait of Hormuz reopens. The International Energy Agency (IEA) emphasized that the unconditional reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is essential to ending the global energy crisis. The Dow Jones surged over 350 points to a record 52,028, and Brent crude oil fell below $80 as the US-Iran peace deal eased global tensions and cooled oil prices to a three-month low. The New York Post called out President Trump over the yet-to-be-revealed Memorandum of Understanding with Iran. European Central Bank officials indicated that peace in Iran alone is not sufficient to fully fix the energy shock. The IEA signaled that oil supply could far outstrip demand growth if the Middle East peace deal holds, potentially leading to an oil glut.</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>The recent US-Iran peace deal marks a significant de-escalation in West Asia, with immediate positive impacts on global energy markets and investor confidence, though its long-term stability and broader geopolitical implications, particularly concerning China's energy strategy, warrant close monitoring. The escalating AI and semiconductor race, characterized by strategic investments, supply chain diversification away from Asia, and stringent US export controls, will continue to define global technological competition and strategic alliances. The confirmed military application of advanced AI by the US in Iran signals a new era of warfare, demanding increased scrutiny of autonomous systems and dual-use technologies. The intensifying global scramble for critical minerals underscores a foundational vulnerability in future energy and technology landscapes, driving both domestic production efforts and international resource plays.</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
